Let the side length of each square be \(3\), so each square has area \(9\).

### Squares I and II
The points have coordinates
\[
P=(1,0),\quad Q=(3,1),\quad R=(2,3),\quad S=(0,2).
\]
The shaded region is the quadrilateral \(PQRS\). In square I, \(PR\) merely divides this same shaded quadrilateral into two triangles, so it does not change its total area.

Each of the four unshaded corner triangles has legs \(1\) and \(2\), hence area
\[
\frac12(1)(2)=1.
\]
Therefore,
\[
S_I=S_{II}=9-4(1)=5.
\]

### Square III
Let the top-right corner be \(W=(3,3)\). Then
\[
U=(1,0),\qquad V=(3,2),\qquad W=(3,3).
\]
The shaded triangle \(UVW\) has base \(VW=1\) and perpendicular height \(2\), so
\[
S_{III}=\frac12(1)(2)=1.
\]

Thus \(5=5>1\), and the comparison is

\[
\boxed{\text{B: }S_I=S_{II}>S_{III}}
\]
